About Us 

 Dorsia is at the forefront of hospitality-tech innovation, redefining how the world gains access to the most in-demand restaurants, events, and experiences. By fusing cutting-edge technology with the art of luxury hospitality, we empower our members to secure impossible-to-get reservations while providing operators with unprecedented levels of control, visibility, and revenue optimization.

 In 2025, we grew revenue 480% and scaled to 400+ venues across 25 destinations, with the launch of our Culture Calendar extending Dorsia beyond restaurants into the world’s most sought-after cultural moments.

 Backed by $54M in funding from investors including Index Ventures, Invus, and Red Sea Ventures, and strategic partners including MoonPay, Major Food Group, and The Dinex Group - Daniel Boulud, we are entering our most consequential phase of growth and reshaping the global hospitality landscape. We’re adding exceptional talent to drive what comes next, and that’s where you come in.

 About the Role 

 Dorsia is seeking an Automation Engineer to sit at the intersection of product quality and operational intelligence. You will own two things that matter equally: ensuring our platform ships reliably through robust automated testing, and identifying the repetitive, manual, and error-prone workflows across the company that should no longer exist.

 The ideal candidate is genuinely product-minded and comfortable operating across the full scope of a problem. You have a bias toward shipping, a low tolerance for toil, and a habit of asking whether something should be automated before accepting that it has to be done by hand.

 What You'll Do 

 Product Quality and Test Automation 

 
 Design, implement, and maintain automated test suites across unit, integration, and end-to-end layers for our core products.

 Own and evolve our test automation framework, including tools like Maestro, Playwright, Cypress, or equivalent API testing approaches.

 Integrate automated tests into the CI/CD pipeline and keep the build signal clean and trustworthy.

 Partner with Engineers and Product Managers to define and validate acceptance criteria for new features before they ship.

 Monitor test runs for flakiness and failures, and drive improvements that fix them durably rather than paper over them.

 Contribute to test strategy and coverage planning, with particular focus on high-risk and high-impact surfaces.

 
 Internal Automation and Tooling 

 
 Proactively identify repetitive, manual, or error-prone workflows across the company, spanning engineering, ops, support, and GTM.

 Design and implement automations using AI tools and LLMs for classification, summarization, routing, and generation; low/no-code platforms like Zapier, Make, n8n, or Retool; and lightweight Python or TypeScript scripts that connect systems together.

 Use AI-assisted coding to prototype quickly, then harden promising prototypes into maintainable, observable production systems.

 Integrate automations with the tools the team already relies on, including Slack, CRMs, ticketing systems, and internal APIs.

 Work with stakeholders to map processes, define requirements, and iterate toward solutions that actually get used.

 
 Reliability, Observability, and Maintenance 

 
 Ensure automations and test systems are reliable, debuggable, and documented well enough that someone else can understand and fix them.

 Implement monitoring and alerting for critical automations, covering error rates, latency, and failure notifications.

 Own the full lifecycle of automations: from idea through prototype, production, iteration, and eventual deprecation.

 Regularly review and prune unused, flaky, or low-value automations to keep the surface area manageable.

 
 Collaboration and Culture 

 
 Work closely with product, engineering, and operations to prioritize what to automate based on actual impact.

 Communicate tradeoffs clearly, build versus buy, and automation complexity versus benefit, without waiting to be asked.

 Help establish an automation-first mindset across the team, encouraging others to think in terms of systems and reusable workflows.

 Share knowledge through documentation and playbooks that are clear enough for non-engineers to follow and build on.

 
 The Winning Recipe 

 
 Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field.

 3-5 years of experience in a QA automation, software engineering, or workflow automation role.

 Strong hands-on experience with test automation frameworks such as Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or equivalent.

 Comfortable writing Python and TypeScript/JavaScript at a level that produces clean, maintainable, production-grade code.

 Experience with CI/CD pipelines and a track record of keeping build signals reliable.

 Demonstrated ability to ship internal automations using low/no-code platforms, LLM-powered tooling, and scripting.

 Solid understanding of APIs and how to connect systems that weren't designed to talk to each other.

 Strong written communication, including documentation that is actually useful long after the sprint ends.

 Ability to work in a fast-paced, complex environment involving cross-functional projects.

 A genuine interest in the Dorsia product, the member experience, and what it means to build for hospitality at this level.

 
 Strong plus: prior experience with reservation system integrations (SevenRooms, Resy, OpenTable), dining payments infrastructure, or luxury/membership consumer apps.

 Compensation and Benefits 

 
 Flexible PTO

 Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 FSA

 Commuter benefits

 Free membership to One Medical

 Teladoc

 Talkspace

 Kindbody

 401(k)

 In-office lunch 3 days a week

 Employee Dining Credits

 
 Salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and stage. We determine our pay by considering skills and experience related to the role, location, and ensuring internal equity relative to other Dorsia employees.
 Compensation: 

 New York Pay Range
 $120,000 — $145,000 USD 


 Workplace Philosophy at Dorsia 

 At Dorsia, we believe that culture eats strategy. The best ideas in the world mean nothing without the right people around the table and the right chemistry between them. We are, unapologetically, a people-first organization. 

 In-Person Matters 

 We’re creating once-in-a-lifetime experiences for the most discerning audience in the world. That doesn’t happen over Zoom. It happens through collisions: a spark across a desk, a kitchen-side conversation that unlocks a partnership, the energy of ideas felt, not typed. That’s why in-office culture is non-negotiable at Dorsia. 

 Who We Hire 

 We don’t subscribe to check-the-box hiring. We hire for merit and mindset, which naturally creates a team with varied backgrounds. What unites us isn’t demographics, it’s a shared vision: to build the social operating system for the cultural vanguard.

 Lifestyle Hours 

 We’re not a 9-to-5 company. Our lifestyle mirrors our members. Early flights, after-work events, and late-night sprints when the work demands it. But we love what we do, and we definitely love a good party.

 High Performance Culture 

 Working at Dorsia isn’t for everyone—and that’s the point. Our culture is designed for builders, not passengers. We move fast, set ambitious standards, and expect people to rise to them. If you have the talent and the drive, this will be a ride to remember.

 A Final Word 

 We’re building something special. It will take long hours and relentless effort. It’s not for everyone. For those with the metabolism, you’ll create something that changes how culture is lived. And that’s the kind of work worth your life’s energy.
